skill.name: video-edit
skill.description: Route video-edit requests to RunComfy models for restyling, background swaps, packaging swaps, motion transfer, and outfit changes. The skill provides model selection guidance, prompt patterns, input fields, and CLI examples for Wan 2.7 Edit-Video, Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control, and Lucy Edit Restyle.
skill.summary: Routes video-edit tasks to the right RunComfy model and supplies matching prompt guidance.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown backticks, schema fields, code fences, hyperlinks, or placeholder URLs rather than executable code. Confirmed risks are intentional RunComfy CLI execution, authenticated third-party media processing, and local API-token storage in a hidden config file. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration instruction was found.

remediation.issue: Global CLI installation and command execution
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted RunComfy CLI versions where possible and require explicit user confirmation before running install, login, or render commands.
Disclose that prompts and media URLs are sent to RunComfy services, and require approval before processing private or regulated media.
Document the token path, permission expectations, token revocation steps, and the RUNCOMFY_TOKEN alternative for CI environments.
Replace https://... examples with clear placeholder tokens or example.com URLs to reduce path-traversal scanner noise.

content.user_title: Edit Videos with RunComfy Model Routing
content.value_statement: Choosing the right video-edit model is slow and error-prone. This skill routes each edit to a RunComfy model and provides matching prompt patterns.
actual_capabilities: Routes general restyle, background swap, and packaging swap requests to Wan 2.7 Edit-Video.
Routes motion-transfer requests to Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control.
Routes lightweight outfit and style edits to Lucy Edit Restyle.
Documents required fields, media limits, resolution options, duration controls, and audio settings.
Provides RunComfy CLI invocation examples for each supported route.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and valid media URLs.
Each route inherits its model duration, resolution, and aspect-ratio limits.
Does not blend multiple RunComfy routes in one edit request.
Prompts and media URLs are processed by RunComfy services.

use_cases.title: Refresh a Talking-Head Clip
use_cases.description: Change a background or lighting style while preserving face, pose, lip movement, and source audio.

use_cases.title: Update Product Presentation
use_cases.description: Swap packaging artwork or product surroundings while keeping the original framing and camera motion.

use_cases.title: Transfer Character Motion
use_cases.description: Apply motion from a reference clip to a target character with identity preservation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a Background Swap
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one source video.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this video with the best RunComfy route. Preserve the subject, motion, lip movement, and audio. Change only the background to a clean office.

prompt_templates.title: Restyle an Outfit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the route that best preserves identity for an outfit change. Keep the face, body motion, and scene framing stable. Change only the clothing style.

prompt_templates.title: Transfer Reference Motion
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced motion-control request with a target character and motion clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the target character media and the reference motion video. Transfer the motion accurately while preserving character identity and avoiding extra style changes.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Route with Constraints
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request when quality, duration, and model limits matter.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the edit goal, media type, duration, resolution need, and audio requirement. Choose one RunComfy route, explain the choice briefly, and prepare a single-direction edit prompt.

output_examples.input: A creator asks to make a short talking-head clip look like a neutral office recording.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Wan 2.7 Edit-Video, leads with face and lip preservation, and requests only the background change.

output_examples.input: A brand team wants new package artwork applied to a handheld product video.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Wan 2.7 Edit-Video with a reference image and keeps hand motion, framing, and audio stable.

output_examples.input: An animator wants a character image to follow dance motion from a reference clip.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control and frames the prompt around motion transfer and identity hold.

best_practices: Put preservation goals before the requested change.
Use one clear edit direction per render.
Confirm media rights, duration limits, and privacy needs before sending URLs.
anti_patterns: Combining background, wardrobe, motion, and packaging changes in one request.
Passing a reference image when the request only needs general restyling.
Sending private or regulated video content without approval.

faq.question: Does this skill edit videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI and RunComfy model services for processing.

faq.question: Which models can it route to?
faq.answer: It routes to Wan 2.7 Edit-Video, Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control, and Lucy Edit Restyle.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects the RunComfy CLI and an authenticated RunComfy account or token.

faq.question: Can it preserve source audio?
faq.answer: Some routes support preserving audio. The skill documents the relevant audio options for those models.

faq.question: Can it process long videos?
faq.answer: No. Each model has duration limits, such as short Wan edits and longer Kling motion-control outputs.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private videos?
faq.answer: Use caution. Prompts and media URLs are sent to RunComfy services, so private content needs approval.
